screen_only_take.verdict: ONE GENERATION BEATS TWO ON A SCREEN-ONLY TAKE. The unedited export keeps green 79.1 % / blue 88.4 % of the source's saturation by copying the raw channel, against 70.3 / 75.2 % by copying the composite — the same picture, one 4:2:0 generation earlier, for strictly less work. THE ONE COST, AND IT IS NOT IN THE TASK'S "free" FRAMING: the download grows 11.4 % (1.52 against 1.36 MB on this take). The COLOUR win is structural and not bought with those bytes — X15(b) measured 3x the bitrate buying 4 % of the fringe on 4:2:0 — but part of the luma dB is. And J6 stops writing 0.17 MB/s — a whole hardware encoder that never runs — while the preview and the frozen-screen detector keep running off the paint.

prod.caveat: Raw-channel drops read 62/60 on the paint take and 55/53 on the record take, one sample each on a machine that was also running this session. G8 measured that a synthetic canvas source hands the encoder BGRA where a real display hands NV12, which dominates that number; an earlier paint take on the same build read 41/36. No direction may be claimed from these. The deterministic numbers are the encoder plan, the Mpx/s and the bytes on disk, all of which the local rig measured against a same-process control.
